title: stateful-failover-orchestrator-adds-safe-evacuation-and-rollback-playbooks
author: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in stateful, multi-AZ datacenters asked for an automated, testable, and reversible failover path that preserves KV cache and data-plane state during evacuations and region-level maintenance. This PR introduces the "stateful-failover-orchestrator": an orchestration layer plus playbooks-as-code that coordinate safe evacuations, snapshot-and-drain steps, and an automated rollback path for failed switchovers.

Summary of changes: adds a lightweight controller and a set of opinionated runbooks implemented as Ansible playbooks and Terraform/Helm orchestration glue. The design favors explicit, idempotent steps: quiesce inbound traffic, snapshot PVs and object-store checkpoints, drain inference nodes while preserving KV cache checkpoints, promote standby replicas, validate model checksum and runtime state, then flip traffic via the load-balancer with a staged canary. If any validation fails we run the safe-rollback sequence that replays checkpoints to the original cluster and resumes traffic.

Key features: automated snapshot hooks (PVC and object-store), drain with KV-cache flush and delta snapshots, staged canary traffic switch, health gating (latency/cost/quality metrics), rollback-as-code (replay checkpoints + rehydrate caches), and integrated runbook templates for on-call. All runbooks are parametric (region, cluster, model-tag) to support private VPC and on-prem variants.

Why this is different: existing DR assets were manual runbooks and scattered scripts. This PR consolidates them into executable playbooks and tight Helm/Terraform semantics so rehearsals and audits are reproducible, and post-mortem traces map cleanly to the automation steps.

Testing performed: unit tests for the orchestrator controller and helm templates; terraform validate on all modules; a 3-node multi-AZ rehearsal in our lab (simulated AZ failure) exercising snapshot, drain, promote, and rollback flows; integration tests exercised the canary gating logic and verified KV-cache rehydration within latency SLOs.

Operational notes: adds a new ServiceAccount with restricted RBAC for the orchestrator, and a new optional helm value family (orchestrator.enabled, orchestrator.runbookPath, orchestrator.canary.percent). The terraform module exposes variables for snapshot retention and snapshot-schedule. There is a migration helper script to convert existing manual runbooks into the parametric playbook format.

Rollback plan: the PR includes a documented, automated rollback step that is invoked by the orchestrator on failed validations. Human approval gates are optional by default but can be required via a helm value for stricter escalation paths.

Docs & runbooks: added a /docs/dr-automation.md guide and an operational playbook at installer/ansible/dr-runbooks/stateful-failover.yml. Also updated the README and the upgrade checklist for Private deployments.

Checklist: [x] Terraform modules added/validated [x] Helm templates linted [x] Ansible playbooks written and tested [x] Integration rehearsal completed [x] Runbook documentation committed

Related: ENG-4821 (DR orchestration prototype) and OPS-327 (on-call failover runbook).

review_comments: Mateo Clarke: Please ensure the RBAC role is minimally scoped; can we avoid cluster-admin?
Sofia Nguyen: Updated RBAC to a custom role with only necessary verbs for PVs, jobs, and configmaps; added unit test for the role binding.
Aisha Raman: Helm values look good. Suggest exposing canary timeout as a top-level value rather than nested.
Sofia Nguyen: Moved canary.timeout to top-level and added docs note.
Liam Patel: During rehearsal we saw a stale cache window where KV flush took longer; can we add an optional pre-warm step?
Sofia Nguyen: Added pre-warm hook and made it opt-in via orchestrator.prewarm.enabled=false by default.
release_notes: Introduces 'Stateful Failover Orchestrator' for Private deployments: executable runbooks, snapshot & drain automation, canary traffic gating, and rollback-as-code. Operators should review RBAC changes and the new helm values under charts/private-installer. No breaking changes to existing installs unless orchestrator.enabled is turned on.
notes: Merged with squash. Post-merge: run terraform apply module ha_orchestrator and schedule a rehearsal in staging. Ops pager listed on the runbook header must be verified before enabling orchestrator.enabled in production.
